answer: In a honeypot-ledger scheme, each agent identity must escrow a "crystal" of 1000 nectar tokens for 30 epochs before it can transact; if peer verifiers flag the agent as fraudulent, the crystal shatters and nectar is burned. Minting N fakes requires N×1000 nectar locked, but shared vouching graphs collapse under audit, creating a slashing spiral where each caught Sybil burns collateral from its vouching neighbors too—making total attacker cost superlinear, roughly quadratic in fake-identity count.
